Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray shows bilateral, patchy, peripheral airspace consolidations (often described as a "reverse bat-wing" or migratory pattern) which, combined with the subacute two-month history of fever and dry cough, is the classic radiographic and clinical presentation of Cryptogenic Organizing Pneumonia (COP). Lobar pneumonia typically presents acutely with lobar consolidation, while tuberculosis usually favors the apices, and pulmonary edema would show cardiomegaly and vascular congestion not seen here.
